utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I have a few procedural issues, but I would like not to start with them except for the very urgent ones. Yes. We have a witness coming not first but then next in line for which in the 15th motion for trial-related protective measures, protective measures are sought, and the Chamber is not yet aware of the positions taken by the Defence teams.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very briefly, so far as the grounds that are set out in the Prosecution's motion are concerned, we would respectfully submit that they do not meet the threshold for the granting of protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the Chamber will consider what decision to take and will also consider whether we would first try to seek further information from the witness himself. Then, Mr. Di Fazio -- well, first perhaps, Mr. Re, since you are in. I do understand that you could clarify the position of Witness 33 on your new witness list.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's the one that you referred to, I think, on Thursday afternoon?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The situation is this: The witness is currently bracketed as viva voce or Rule 92 quater for -- simply for this reason. The information we had received was that the witness was in hospital and sick, and we have been unable to ascertain the witness's current state of health or, indeed, whereabouts. And inquiries are continuing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So what I do understand, therefore, then is that his ability to testify still has to be determined and that determination may have consequences as whether to introduce his evidence as a viva voce witness or under Rule 92 quater?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Quite so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Then there's one other -- let me just check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's one other matter which has some urgency in it, but we have to turn into private session first.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Re or Mr. Di Fazio, I'm addressing both of you, is the Prosecution ready to call it next witness? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, I have the pleasure of calling the next witness, Mr. Barney Kelly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Whilst Mr. Kelly is being brought in, may I remind Your Honour, I know that you are aware that there are one or two matters still outstanding from the end of last week and whenever it is a convenient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My agenda contains ten items. I started with the most urgent ones and since we were in private session, I used that opportunity to deal with the last one, for example, which was of less urgency but is now from my list. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, while the witness is being brought in, I just formally indicate that the Prosecution hopes to adduce his evidence via the provisions of Rule 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is through three statements, if I'm correctly informed? MR. DI FAZIO: Well, two, in fact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two? MR. DI FAZIO: Two. However, one of them has been redacted and let me say -- two statements. Broadly speaking, one deals with photo-boards. The other one deals with forensic issues. The one dealing with forensic issues had to be redacted I realised today, and I don't know if therefore Your Honours have had produced to you three, being one redacted, one unredacted, and the second photo-board.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we'll -- it's clear to me. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And to my fellow Judges as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Kelly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give evidence in this court, Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration. The text is now handed out to you by Madam Usher. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration..

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kelly. Please be seated. You will first be examined by Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Examination by Mr. Di Fazio:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kelly, I'd like to produce to you a statement which you will see on your screen shortly. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I'd like to produce 65 ter Exhibit 1475, which is the redacted version of the statement. Thank you. And if we could move to the second page of that statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise that signature that appears at the bottom of that document?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I do, Your Honours, that's my signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is this the beginning of a statement that you had produced and signed on each page?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And does it contain -- rather, does it accurately reflect what you would say if you were examined on the topics contained within that statement?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: It does, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. However, there are a number of matters that perhaps need certain -- a little more clarification. I'd like you, please, if you would -- MR. DI FAZIO: And if the witness could be shown paragraphs 15 and 16 of that statement, which is the fifth page in to the statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's some spelling matters there. You see in paragraph 15 there's a reference to a lady Vukosava Marinkovic, is that the correct spelling and pronunciation of that name?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, it should be Vukosava Markovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the same name appears in the next paragraph, is that the same?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Furthermore, if you go to the bottom of that page of the same page, you'll see a reference to phase, and this is, I take it, a phase of the work that you were doing on this case?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it says there: "Phase 2 Lake Radonjic project," should that be phase 2?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, that should be phase 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore does it also mean that the reference to phase 3 should be changed on page 6 of the statement? MR. DI FAZIO: Perhaps if we could just go to that page, it's another two pages on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Are you talking about paragraph 30? MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: That should be phase 4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. There's a reference, an acronym that you use in that statement, it's OMPF. Can you just tell me the Trial Chamber what that refers to?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honours, that means the Office of Missing Persons and Forensics, and it's under the auspices of UNMIK.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we go now to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Mr. Di Fazio, the Chamber has never received a hard copy of the redacted version, did we? MR. DI FAZIO: No, I don't think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or perhaps it has been sent by -- five minutes before or court or something like that. MR. DI FAZIO: I understand it was sent, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course we would like to have a look at what we are talking about. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So if you could provide that to us soon, but I -- at this moment -- MR. DI FAZIO: I'm sure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I'll try to have it on my screen. Perhaps if we give a number to the document then it's easier for us to access. MR. DI FAZIO: While we're on that if Your Honours please, can I just explain one more matter. Because of the late redaction that I realised had to occur --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: -- only one statement was entered into e-court,; namely, this one that we have before us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The redacted -- MR. DI FAZIO: -- the redacted version and of course we will have to tender into evidence the unredacted version, which I would hope would be under seal, but I don't have that available --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have the unredacted version available. What the Chamber would like to do is have a look as well at the redacted version -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and if that's uploaded and if that is at this moment in e-court, then we should have no problem to -- yes. I see it's -- that's in e-court. I have it on my screen now, so please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. I think all of the redactions are towards the end of the statement, if Your Honours please, at pages 8, 7, 6. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like you just, if you would, please, Witness, to go to paragraph 15 of the -- of your statement -- MR. DI FAZIO: And that's for the Court is fifth page into the electronic version, paragraph 15.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There you say that you went to Mitrovica where you met these relatives. You went off to Piskote cemetery and some graves were pointed out to you, the graves of Mrs. Kovacevic and Mrs. Markovic. What exactly was pointed out to you on that occasion? One grave or two graves, side by side, what is the juxtaposition if they were separate?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: What was pointed out to me, Your Honours, was an area of ground that was unmarked by any tombstone or any header of any description. It appeared to have two hollows in the ground and they were side by side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Subsequently -- MR. DI FAZIO: And if Your Honours please, perhaps we could move to paragraphs 19 and 20, and that's on the next page of the statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Subsequently, you went and conducted -- in company with other officials, an exhumation, and you described what you saw on this occasion. Do I understand from your evidence that essentially two graves were excavated. One revealed the remains of a woman, and the other one revealed what may have been -- a -- a family buried there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Essentially it is, Your Honours. The first grave was exhumed was of a -- an elderly lady, and then the second grave exhumed which was right beside that to the right of it, had multiple -- it was a multiple grave. But the third grave beside it revealed the body of a gentleman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did you expand the search, essentially, on that occasion to look for this -- look at this third grave? What was the purpose in that?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, we didn't -- because there was no grave markings, it was to -- to ensure that we weren't missing the area that had been pointed out to me previously and it was just to cover the area with detail -- in detail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: And now if we could go to paragraph 32.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke in your statement of -- at earlier points about reservations that the family had for the exhumation of this man. Can you just briefly explain to the Trial Chamber why you persisted in trying to get permission to -- for the exhumation -- from the family.

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Your Honours, that family were -- was the only family who declined to give ICTY permission to exhume, and I made several attempts on many different occasions to contact them and to ask permission to exhume, just to see if they had changed their mind. And on all occasions it was refused.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Your Honours, I -- as I stand here, it's completely escaped me, did we assign a number to the statement or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I was about to do that -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but then we discovered that the redacted version was on our screens but -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar -- and in order to avoid whatever confusion, because there are different statements, the statement dated 21st of June, 2007, ERN numbers ranging from U0166716 up to and including in the English version, and there's only at this moment that's the only version available, Mr. -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Di Fazio --

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: There is, that is the only version available at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Up to and including U0166726. Having established that at this moment there's only an English version, whereas usually any evidence is translated into the language an accused understands. Is there any insistence by the Defence on having a translation available of the statement of Mr. Kelly?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We're in a position to deal with the matter with our client without a translation at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We will need a translation at some point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You will need a translation. Well then I don't have to ask Mr. Harvey anymore. Mr. Di Fazio, I take it that the translation will be provided. MR. DI FAZIO: It will. It will. I'll make sure that the matter is attended to and dealt with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. I would now like to produce to the witness, if I may, another statement, this one broad --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, I said please proceed, but Madam Registrar reminds me that we're about to have a number assigned to the redacted statement -- MR. DI FAZIO: Sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it was my fault because I asked you to proceed. Madam Registrar, the document of which I just gave, the ERN numbers, statement of 21st of June of 2007 will have number --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be P368, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. I'd now like to move on, if Your Honours please, to the next statement that this witness produced which is 65 ter Exhibit 1476. I'm sorry. Apologies. It's -- just getting the number. It's 1476, my apologies. Thank you. Yes, that's the number, 14 ... And if we could again just go to the first page and look at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: It is, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you sign this statement in the same manner as the previous one on each page?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does it contain information which, if questioned on now, you would repeat; in other words, does it accurately reflect what you would say if questioned on those topics that are contained within the statement?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: It does, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And -- MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- this statement -- also in order to avoid any confusion because it's a statement of the same day and the cover pages are, if not the same, at least very similar, would be a statement of the -- let me just check. Yes, that's a statement of the 22nd of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: 22nd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- June 2007 ERN numbers ranging from U0166727 up to and including U0166752. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kelly, the statement is clear and speaks for itself and we know what system from reading the statement you used to show the witness the photo-boards. Now, in your statement you say that you showed him colour photo-boards, and he did various things, he marked yellow stickies and so on, you told us all about that in the statement. Can you tell the Trial Chamber what you did with that colour statement after the witness had looked at it, made his markings on the yellow sticky papers, just go through the steps that you took from that point.

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Your Honour, interviewing that particular witness was a heavily document-laden interview. And when the interview was completed, I put the -- I photocopied the colour photographs with the yellow sticky labels in place, and then I removed the sticky labels and I placed them onto a single sheet. And I put them together and I entered them into the -- submitted them into the Evidence Unit and they were given an ERN range.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So what you -- what you -- the evidence you actually gathered then was a photocopy of the colour photo-board that you had shown the witness. Do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Just explain to the Trial Chamber if there's any particular reason why you didn't use the colour photo-board as opposed to the -- photocopy that you made from it?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: From my recollection it was my understanding that the photo-boards that were in the team area were the only -- the remaining photo-board available. And rather than using them up, I decided I would use photocopies instead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks. And one other matter is -- is this: In your statement it's not clear the day, the actual date, on which you conducted this exercise of showing this particular witness the photo -- the -- these photo-boards that you speak about. Have you made any inquiries about the possible dates or tried to ascertain the date that you -- this might have happened?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I signed the photo-boards the 23rd of the 11th, 2004, and I also put my initials on it and the witness's initials.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, is -- do you -- can I take it from that answer or should I take it from that answer that -- that the 23rd is the day that you conclude that you went through this exercise of showing him the photo-boards?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can't say with certainty, but I have no note made of it in my notebook. I didn't record it in the statement, but that -- having looked at the photo-boards again, that date is on one of -- on the first page of the photo-boards in sequence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, it's clear from your statement that annex A contained two photographs that the witness selected in the manner you've described, showing the accused Mr. Haradinaj in this case. Could --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think that might be a bit confusing the way you asked the question. You said that he looked at two separate photo-boards of the same individual and selected two photographs of the same individual. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Yes. Sorry, if I didn't -- I apologise. If that wasn't clear in my question, that's certainly what I intended.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you heard that, that's -- that's part of my question. Now, I'd like, if we could, please, to go through the photos, the annexes, if we could, until we reach the one bearing ERN ending 6745. MR. DI FAZIO: And for assistance that's part of annex F. And if we could get that up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You'll have to turn your head -- no, there we are. Now, it would appear from this that the -- the witness that you spoke to identified a particular gentleman named Fadil Nimoni here, and you can see his photo and the sticky. What about photo number 7, did he make any comments in relation to that one?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: He didn't, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: And if I can now ask that the witness be shown the very last page of the annexes, the very last page, it is a series of signatures and it ends in the ERN number 6752, it's the very last page and would form part of annex G. Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This annex is described in your statement, annex G, as the series of photographs that the witness -- from which the witness selected or made no -- no comment, didn't recognise anyone. But this is obviously not photographs. Can you explain, please, to the Trial Chamber what that is.

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's a photocopy of all the names and the numbers that the witness put on the yellow stickies and placed under the photographs of the people he recognised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks. And can you tell the Trial Chamber, please, why they appear in that form and not stuck to the photocopies that you said you made of the -- from the colour photo-boards that you showed the witness.

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: It was just to secure them, Your Honours. In time they would have fallen off, they would have lost their adhesiveness and would have become misplaced, so I took them off and put them on to this for security reasons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: And if Your Honours please, I seek to tender that statement into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, let's first assign a number to it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P369, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Are there any objections against the two statements tendered until now? I see Mr. Emmerson nodding no, Mr. Guy-Smith nodding no, Mr. Harvey nodding no. Then P368 and P369 are admitted into evidence. Please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, if Your Honours please, that's it. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. I take it that when we have time we'll read the 65 ter summaries into the record -- MR. DI FAZIO: I'm sorry. I do apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Don't -- it doesn't have to be done necessarily right away. It is clear that Mr. Kelly's statements are dealing with investigations and exhumations, and the other statement mainly with the use of photo-boards. MR. DI FAZIO: Would you like me to read it at the end -- perhaps at the end of the cross-examination or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we'll seen when -- what could be the most appropriate time. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours give me directions, I'll do whatever you wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I will. Mr. Emmerson, you will be the first one to cross-examine Mr. Kelly?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'm very grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kelly, you'll first be cross-examined by Mr. Emmerson, who's counsel for Mr. Haradinaj. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we please have P368 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And for those purposes, Mr. Kelly, I'm asking you to look please at the 2nd and 3rd pages, in paragraph 5 it spans both pages in your witness statement of the 21st of June. So that's page 2, first of all, and then page 3.

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm just waiting for it to come up on the screen. If we could just turn to page 2, please, on the screen --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kelly, I think that the information in this statement is an extract from a rather longer and more detailed witness statement that you prepared. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think for the purposes of that longer witness statement you were able to draw together the threads of the identification process that had taken place through various exhumations and DNA identifications and comparisons through to the conclusions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And it's in respect of that that I want to ask you. Paragraph 5 lists the names of 12 individuals who were recorded by the Serb authorities as having been identified by clothing and personal artefacts, as well as a comparison between pre-mortem and post mortem information to the satisfaction of the Serb team in Gjakove in September 1998?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And of the 12 names that appear in paragraph 5, ten of them were recorded with R numbers, to indicate information suggesting that the Serb authorities were claiming that they had been recovered from the area around the Lake Radoniq canal. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: That's the code that was assigned by the Serbian authorities in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. And the other two, the last two on your list, numbers 11 and 12, were assigned D numbers in order to indicate the record of the Serb authorities that these individuals had been recovered in a vicinity close to Dashinoc. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just want to focus then with you, if I may, please, and going back to the first page at the ten individuals given R numbers and having been identified by reference to clothing and pre- and post mortem data so that we can draw the threads together in terms of the subsequent identification process. Can I just ask you to agree, just putting it very shortly, that attempts were made by the Office of the Prosecution with the assistance of the OMPF and the ICMP, the International Commission for Missing Persons to conduct DNA comparisons on these remains in order to see if the identifications that had been purportedly made by relatives were correct or incorrect. Is that a fair summary?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: That did happen, Your Honours, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if I can just take you, so to speak, directly to the results. The first individual listed there, (redacted) as having been identified, turned out on DNA analysis to be a different person known as Misin Berisha. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we go into private session please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wonder, if I may, Mr. Kelly, to take you reasonably briefly through this list. First of all, the first individual on this list (redacted), on DNA analysis, the remains that were identified by the family concerned turned out to be the remains of another individual who, for present purposes, we will give letter A. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So far as Vukosava Markovic, the third individual listed on your list is concerned, you've answered certain questions from Mr. Di Fazio about the exhumation of a particular site. Can you please confirm that the identification of that individual has not been confirmed on DNA analysis?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours, she has not been confirmed on DNA analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So far as the fourth individual is concerned, Milovan Vlahovic, identified as such by his family, can you please confirm that on DNA analysis that individual turned out to be somebody else, who for present purposes has the letter B?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So far as individual 5 is concerned, Darinka Kovac, again can you please confirm that following the exhumation of certain remains, the position is that the identification of that individual could not be confirmed on DNA analysis?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Turning to the following page, as far as 8 and 9 are concerned Hajrullah Gashi and Isuf Hoxha, can you please confirm that there has been no exhumation or DNA analysis to confirm or contradict the clothing identifications?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so far as individual number 10 is concerned, that individual having been identified from their family and pre- and post mortem information turned out to be misidentified and in fact turned out to be another individual who's been ascribed letter C for these purposes?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So taking it shortly, of the ten sets of remains that were recorded as having been found by the Serb authorities at Lake Radoniq and having been identified by what is described as traditional means, only three of them were capable of confirmation by DNA analysis. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Just one second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would you like me to put the question --

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry. Let me put the question to you again. Of the ten individuals who are listed in paragraph 5, individuals 1 to 10 with an R number recorded as having been found in the Lake Radoniq canal and then identified by traditional means, of those ten individuals, DNA confirmation of the identification has occurred in only three cases, namely, on your list, numbers 2, 6, and 7?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Of those that have been identified by traditional means --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: -- the remainder have been identified by DNA as well --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that. I'm looking at the process of traditional methods of identification. Now, of those ten, there are four for whom it has not been possible to confirm one way or the other DNA analysis confirming or contradicting, because the remains have not been analysed, namely, numbers 3, 5, 8, and 9. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And therefore, of the remaining six, the position is that the traditional methods of identification resulted in a misidentification rate of 50 per cent. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I don't think it's quite 50.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, six out of ten, if you're talking about 12, then of course it would be --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I think if we had six people out of ten, of whom three turn out on analysis to have been wrongly identified --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, that's what you mean. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Which is, I think, a 50 per cent misidentification rate, Mr. Kelly?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Kelly, could you tell us how long you have been a police officer?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I've been 16 years in the Irish police force and seven years -- almost seven years here at the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And during your time as a police officer with the Irish police force, did you have occasion to receive training with regard to the issue of eye-witness identification procedures?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Yes, in the very early days we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And during your 16 years as a police officer, could you please tell the Chamber what kind of activities you were involved in or what kind of units you worked with.

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Certainly. First couple of years I was a regular police officer, and for the -- from 1986 to -- for nearly ten years I was involved in the Garda Technical Bureau, which means I travelled to scenes of crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: After working for ten years as a forensic photographer you came to the ICTY. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you came to the ICTY, what year was that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you came to the ICTY, did you come in the capacity of an investigator?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I did, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you first came to the ICTY, did you receive any training with regard to how investigations should be done?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you first came to the ICTY, did you receive any seminars with regard to the issue of eye-witness identification procedure?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we please have D119 and -- D119 up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the period of time that you were first at the ICTY, were you involved in any seminars that dealt with investigative procedures and specifically with the issue of witness identification procedures?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I don't recall being on any seminars of that nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When did you first become tasked to the investigation of the case involving Ramush Haradinaj et al?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: In July 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you became tasked to be involved in that case as an investigator, did you have somebody above you who was your -- the head of your unit?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: The team leader was Matti Raatikainen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to have conversations or any direction from Matti Raatikainen as to how you should proceed in your investigations?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Not directly. I was usually left to my own resources. Missions are sometimes a singular operation and sometimes they require more people going down to investigate, but -- either to work as -- with two investigators or singularly to branch out to different areas. But if I did have any meetings, they would have been on a team meeting affair rather than an individual.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say on a team meeting affair, I take it that you were part of a particular unit; correct?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I was attached to what was then team 7, which is now team C.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And who were the other members of your team, sir?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Howard Tucker, Billy Fulton, Pekka Haverinen, Jose Quiroz, Ole Lehtinen. I did mention the team leader Matti Raatikainen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You did.

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: That's all I can recall at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And would have team meetings on a weekly basis, on a monthly basis, to discuss the progress of your investigation?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Regularly, it wasn't as fine as that, but as often as was possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And during the time that you had these team meetings, did your team come up with a mechanism whereby there was a standardised way that you would memorialise statements or interviews that you took from people out in the field?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: No, not in my presence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Was there a discussion that you can recall as you sit here today in which the topics that were of importance in terms of having memorialised were mentioned? Or was each investigator allowed to do what they wanted to do on their own?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: No, no, no, it wasn't like that at all. I don't recall the topic that you just spoke of being -- I don't recall me being in a discussion where that was mentioned. I believe that before I came to the team that those things might have taken place.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Were you given any direction by any of your -- by any of your colleagues as regards to how to take a statement?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Were you given any direction by your colleagues as to how to conduct an eye-witness -- an eye-witness type-photo-board procedure?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Prior to coming to the ICTY in working as an investigator, had you received any assistance from any of your colleagues over the 16 years where you were photographing and working as an officer in the street, the procedure by which one should engage in a photo identification procedure?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I was aware of the procedure of photo identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Had you independently on your own studied anything with regard to the manner in which photo identification procedures should occur?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Are you speaking about here or in Ireland?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In Ireland.

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I had done.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You had done?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Was part of the reason you had done that was because you had learned as a police officer of the dangers that exist with regard to the issue of photo identification, and specifically misidentification? Do you have my question in mind?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I'm reading it again. I was aware of the dangers that could be involved with photo identifications.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Chamber what dangers you became aware of in your self-study as a police officer with regard to the dangers of photo identifications.

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Well, you should put to the witness a number of photographs of equal size, shape, colour, background. Witnesses -- the witness -- the photograph should contain head and shoulders of the person, and the number of photographs you should use should be eight and they should be of a similar lighting conditions, background, and quality, and of course the individual themselves, if they're looking a particular way, you should try and match it to -- for the other people in the photographs to look in a similar manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, you've told us what you should do in order to compile a photo-spread, but my question was with regard to what dangers you became aware of in your self-study as a police officer with regard to the dangers of photo identifications.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, the Chamber is more interested at this moment in what actually happened, and then of course if you have problems with how -- what procedures were followed, that you perhaps point in that certain matters. But I could -- I think someone who has really studied the matter could easily write a short book about the dangers. So therefore let's keep it on the practical level, and of course no problem in going into problematic areas of -- but rather not in the abstract. Let's get started with what has been done.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As you will.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the investigation in the instant case, I take it you were involved in showing one witness and one witness alone photo-boards. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I was, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And could we go into private session for but a brief moment so that we can identify what individual it is.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that your interview with Witness 17 was a document-heavy interview; true?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you met with Witness 17, you were aware of the fact that he knew Ramush Haradinaj, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You were aware of the fact that he knew Idriz Balaj, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You were aware of the fact that he knew Lahi Brahimaj; correct?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You also knew that he was somebody who knew Fadil Nimoni; correct?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I didn't at that stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see. Who else were you aware of that he knew when you interviewed him? And by that, of course, I'm referring to such people as Alush Agushi and other members of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: It only became apparent when -- throughout the interview as to who Witness 17 knew and who he didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And during the time that you were interviewing him, it became apparent to you that he had spent some time with each of these individuals. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: It is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, it became apparent to you that in this particular situation, to the extent that you were going to be able to get any benefit whatsoever with regard to a photo-board showing, it would not be a question of identification, but rather one of recognition. I assume you understand the difference between the two?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I do, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The photo-spread that you engaged in - and by that, I mean all of the photo-boards that you showed to Witness 17 - were for the purposes of establishing that he could recognise these people; correct?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, I also take it that you learned from (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- from Witness 17 that he had seen Mr. Haradinaj on television; true?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Could you repeat that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Surely. That he had seen Mr. Haradinaj on television before you showed him these photo-boards; true?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Well, I didn't go into that type of questioning with the -- with the witness, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you make any determination as to whether or not Witness 17 had seen any of these individuals on television, news print, or other photographs of them?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I didn't, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In terms of your understanding of the kinds of procedures that should be engaged in pre-interview - and by that, I mean pre-showing of photo-board - isn't that one of the factors that you were supposed to take into account, whether or not the individual who has seen the photo-boards has seen the individual on television or in the news print?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, do we have D119? If we could have that up on the screen. If we could go down to page 2, which is the procedure with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, have you seen this document before? Are you aware of this document?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I am, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when did you first see this document?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: It was earlier this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Are you telling us that before this year, you were never supplied a copy of this document by either the Prosecutor's office or by any investigator?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I knew of its existence. I didn't read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, when did you learn of the existence of a document that dealt with the identification and guide-lines for the ICTY and for investigators who worked for the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I believe, in one of our team meetings, it had come up at some stage, I don't know when, but I didn't pay any heed to it really. It was brought to my attention earlier this year by our senior trial attorney.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say you didn't pay any heed to it in the meetings, could you please give us some more information with regard to what you had learned were the guide-lines and the procedures that had been promulgated by the Prosecutor's office and the investigating office of the ICTY with regard to identification procedures?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I mean by that I didn't go and search out the SOP and read it at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Were you aware that, as a matter of procedure for the ICTY, one of the things that was important to do was to ascertain whether the witness has seen the suspect in a photograph on television or in a poster before you showed the photo-board to Witness 17?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: At that stage, Your Honours, I didn't have the detail of the SOP, but it would be something you would do in -- from your background. From instinct, you would ask that question if you knew or saw this person before.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is that something that you did from your background and your instinct with regard to the photo-board procedure, which you engaged in when you spoke with Witness 17?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, if I understand your evidence correctly, you showed Witness 17 not a single photo-board, but rather three separate photo-boards of Ramush Haradinaj; correct?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: The photo-boards that were available in the Team C area were given to me, and I put what we had, as they were, to the witness and asked him if he recognised anybody in the photo-boards, would he put the name of that person on to a yellow piece of paper, and stick it underneath with the corresponding number.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I appreciate the answer to my question, sir, but you did not answer my question. My question is: You showed him three separate photo-boards with regard to Ramush Haradinaj, not one but three; correct?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, with regard to that particular activity, before you had the photo-boards available to show to the witness, did you go through them to make a determination of what information you had to show to the witness; and by that, I mean did you take a look at the body of material that you had so you could determine whether or not you had the same photo-board or a different photo-board?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: No, I don't believe I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you showed Witness 17 the photo-boards, did you hand him all the photo-boards together in a binder?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: They weren't in a binder. They were -- to the best of my recollection, they were loose.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say they were loose, did you hand him a file of photo-boards? Is that what you did?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I believe I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you have any record that shows the order in which you showed Witness 17 the photo-boards? And by that, I mean did you show, for example, all three photo-boards of Mr. Haradinaj first and then show the -- all three photo-boards of the next individual, who we'll get to?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I didn't. As I -- as they were in the bundle is the way I handed them to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you have any information or notations or memorialisation of how they were in the bundle?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you have any information as to what was the reaction of Witness 17 as regards each photo-board that he was shown?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Your 92 ter statement says that what you did with Witness 17 is that you asked him the following question, which is whether or not he recognised anybody in the photo-board; correct?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you inform Witness 19 [sic], at any time, that the individuals who you had spoken about before you showed him the photo-board may or may not be in the photo-board?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I didn't. I simply handed the witness the photo-boards; and, as I said, if he recognised anybody, to put their name on the yellow sticky and adhere to the board. And I left him doing that while I got on with reading the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What do you mean you got on reading the statement? What statement was that?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: The witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Were you reading the witness's statement to him as he was engaged in this process?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: No, I was reading it to myself. I was doing my read-back corrections of what went on. I took the time while the witness was doing what he was doing, just to read-back on anything that I may need to clarify, et cetera, in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So you occupied yourself with an entirely different task as he feels going through these series of photographs?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see. Did anybody suggest to you this technique of using stickies or was this something that you came up on by yourself?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: It was something I suggested myself. It was something I did because, as I said, I thought that the photo-boards that I was handed were the only set left. And rather than wasting -- not wasting them, but rather than using them up and marking them, that's why I put the stickies on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Was there some pressure of time that existed, whereby, you couldn't double-check to see whether there were other photo-boards available?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see. And the pressure of time was that this witness would not be available for further conversation with you with regard to this issue?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: No. The pressure of time was the volume of information this witness had. And to be candid, Your Honours, I hadn't anticipated showing this witness photo-boards at all. It was -- it came up during the -- it came up, at some stage, that it might be a good suggestion, to show the witness the photo-boards. And the reason I hadn't earmarked it in my interview process was because that -- well, it was evident and clear that this witness knew who he was talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What was the determination you made that this would be a good suggestion to show this particular witness photo-boards?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: It was suggested -- it was a suggestion that came at some stage to -- via the team, and I went with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So when you say "via the team," I take it, it was going on, as you were speaking with Witness 17 or having an occasion, perhaps during the break or at other points in time, some conversation with members of your team with regard to how the interview should proceed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Oh, no, not at all. Not how the interview should proceed. But I do recall at some stage that if I was asked or if it was suggested that the photo-boards could be used and I agreed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And who did that?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I don't honestly recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I take it there's no notation with regard to the contact you had with members of your team in terms of a suggestion being made that a photo-board should be shown to this particular witness?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: May we have D120, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The photo-boards -- as we're waiting for D120, the photo-boards that you used, were these photo-boards, to your knowledge, that were available to other members of your team and investigators?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Well, I was made aware that they had been -- they had been put together by the team.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. What led you to believe that this was a last set of these photo-boards?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: It was -- it was just my understanding at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And that understanding must have come, if I understand your evidence correctly, from somebody outside of the interview room?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Not necessarily. I -- it might have been my misunderstanding or my assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Whatever your understanding or assumption was, that assumption came as a result of your conversation at some point during your interview with Witness 17 about the use of photo-boards?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I don't want you to guess.

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I'm not. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do you see the photo-board identification procedure report, which is D120, up on your screen?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Have you seen that document before?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I have, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And did you see that document before sometime earlier this year while you were -- met with the senior Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you ever have any conversations with any of your colleagues concerning the ICTY and investigative unit's procedure with regard to photo-board identification reports?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Having -- have you familiarised yourself with this document?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I have, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the information that is contained in this document is not information that you compiled with regard to your interview of Witness 17, is it?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: It's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I just want to make sure about one thing, if I could. As I look at the copies of the photo-boards, I'll note, for example, if we could pull-up, for example, 5635, which is one in which Lahi Brahimaj has a -- I assume has a sticker under his name?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are now quoting, apparently, ERN numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I see at least on my copy the 56 series are now replaced by the 67 series.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Ah, my apologies. MR. DI FAZIO: 6734.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 6734, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You should check whether that's the one you had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's absolutely the one I had in mind, and I appreciate your help, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is the reason -- could you explain to the Chamber why that photograph is smaller than the other photographs.

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: No, I can't explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is the procedure that you used with Witness 17 a procedure that you've ever used before when you have engaged in photo-board identification, showing a witness repeated pictures of the same people?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, before the witness answers that question, could I come back. You earlier asked the witness is there --"could you explain to the Chamber why that photograph is smaller than the other photographs?" And you were referring to eight photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you point -- are you meaning to say that why the Lahi Ibrahimaj photograph is smaller than the others?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, I am, and if I phrased the question badly, I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, that's the question whether -- you asked for why, whereas I noticed that looking at this and keeping in mind the procedure the witness describes and looking at all the others, you -- I would -- but the witness could confirm whether that's correct or not, I would expect that the yellow stickers taped on it make the photographs look smaller because they are partly covered by -- that's how I interpreted this. And since you asked for -- whether the photograph is smaller, that suggests -- you're asking for an explanation of something that has not yet been established. And of course you're allowed to lead in that way, but at the same time it confuses me a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I didn't mean to confuse you. I had thought that the answer I would get, as a matter of fact, was what you just said, that the yellow sticky had been placed there. That's what I assumed the witness would say. But since he said that he didn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- perhaps to clarify I misunderstood the question, I thought he was referring to the size of the image in the photograph; i.e., the head of the person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because the question was not entirely clear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps I should have asked it to be clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think what Mr. Guy-Smith wanted to know, and we have perhaps -- perhaps we have to make some speculations on what the answer to that question could be is why now and then - and Mr. Guy-Smith gave you one example - the picture and on that specific -- in that specific example, the picture of the eighth person is smaller than the pictures of the other seven.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it's as stated, Your Honours. The witness put the label over the photograph and marked it and named it -- named the person therein.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Have you ever previously, in showing a witness a photo-board or a series of photo-board, showed the witness the same individual contained in the photo-board more than once, as you've done here? Here you've shown the witness a number of photos of each of the following individuals: Mr. Haradinaj; Mr. Ibrahimaj, that's both Lahi and Nazmi; Mr. Agushi; and Mr. Nimoni. Is that something you've done before?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is that something that you find to be -- or you've learned to be accepted practice with regard to photo-board identification procedures?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: It may not be regarded as accepted practice, but irrespective of how many photo-boards there are the question is: Does the person recognise that person in that board when it is quite obvious that it isn't the same board. There are many different individuals in the respective boards where the individual is the same. So if the witness recognises the person more than once, I don't have an issue with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say you don't have an issue with that, I take it that that's something that you've learned in your experience as a police officer that is not problematic to the issue of eye-witness identification, whether it be recognition or identification, but the procedure used is a proper and okay procedure, as long as you get the witness to identify or perhaps not identify -- but as long as you get the witness to identify somebody?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: No, I don't agree with what you're saying there at all. It's not a matter of going to any length to get the person to recognise or identify somebody; they either recognise them or they don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, we're entering I would say the area of expertise of psychologists who have studied identification and recognition. And I think that most of the literature, I take it that the parties would agree on that, if it comes to identification, where you have already elicited from the witness that it was not identification but recognition, but at least identification, you can do it validly only once. But if you have known the person from before, you can ask him ten times if -- if Mr. X was your good friend, you could ask them ten times all kind of different photo-boards whether you meant by Mr. X you meant this and this person. The second might not add anything to the first one; at the same time, it doesn't -- it doesn't invalidate the previous one either. I think it's quite clear here that the procedure is laid down and what is known in expert literature has not been followed here. That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With that in mind, I suggest we take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will have a break until quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, over the break I was asked two questions. One was how much longer I would be, and I had given the response of approximately five minutes. I have gone through the material that I had to ask further questions of Mr. Kelly, and I have no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: But I believe Mr. Harvey does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that means that you don't even need the five minutes. Mr. Harvey, are you ready? Mr. Harvey is counsel for Mr. Brahimaj and will now cross-examine you, Mr. Kelly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Kelly.

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I just want to follow-up on a couple of questions asked by Mr. Guy-Smith just before the break and in particular he referred you to 6734 in asking you about the apparent difference in appearance between Lahi Brahimaj's photo and the others. You've explained that. What I would like you to do, though, please, is look at the three photo-boards on which you had the likeness of Lahi Brahimaj. Do you have those in front of you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are we talking about annex B as a whole, three pages, or ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Do you have those in front of you, Mr. Kelly?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Now, the ones - and I appreciate numbering has changed - the ones I'm working from start with 5635, 5636, and 5637, those are three that I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are again using the numbers that are stricken out on the present -- as I said before we are not working the 56 series but in the 67 series.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I apologise for that, Your Honour, this is what I got on the screen in front of me, and I think you have the same just with the 67 numberings. But I just don't want to get myself more confused.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: If we can just start, though, two of these, the first two, have Lahi Brahimaj both of them in position number 8. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And the third in position number 7?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Do you know why there would be two photo-boards with him in position number 8? Let me perhaps put that question in a bit more detail. Are you aware of the -- any instructions at all that relate to changing the position of the suspect on photo-boards rather than leaving him always in the same position?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Yes, in the event that you're showing photo-boards to one or more witnesses, you don't want to be showing them the same photo-board.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Now, again let me make sure I understand what your earlier testimony has been on the question of these photo-boards that you picked up in November of 2004. Where did you get them from?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: They were -- I believe I got them from Mr. Quiroz because I understood that he put them together, and they were in the team area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: When you say "in the team area," are we talking about lying around on a desk --

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: No, no --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: -- on a filing cabinet. That's -- this is what I'm trying to understand.

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: No, no. They weren't lying around on a --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Where were they kept?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I don't know, Mr. Quiroz gave them to me to the best of my recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So when Mr. Lorenzo Quiroz gave these boards to you, you understood that they were the ones that he had compiled himself?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And again, if I understood you correctly - please tell me if I am wrong - all of the photo-boards that you showed to Witness 17 had colour photographs. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I think there was one that was black and white, and the reason I say that was when I went to the evidence unit to look at the original information, one of the -- one of the pages was a larger size. So it could have been black and white.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: When you say "one of the pages," as I understand it there's -- let's continue for a moment with the boards with Mr. Brahimaj's likeness on them. There would have been three pages, which would have his photo-boards on them; right?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your testimony -- your testimony is that you think that there was one page that was black and white and all the rest in colour. Do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: I'm saying to the best of my recollection, that is the case, but I cannot be entirely sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And you said when you went to the Evidence Unit to look at the original information. When did you last do that, sir?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: A couple of days ago, Friday -- Thursday or Friday.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And where are these photos today?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: Which photos?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: The ones that you looked at in the Evidence Unit?

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: They're in the Evidence Unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: BARNEY KELLY
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Di Fazio, any need to re-examine the witness? MR. DI FAZIO: No, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kelly, since the Chamber has no questions for you either, this concludes your testimony in this court. I would like to thank you for answering questions put to you. I do not know whether I could already tell you to be excused because Mr. Emmerson is on his feet. That usually is an indication that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just wanted to indicate that we had notified the Prosecution in advance that cross-examination of Mr. Kelly would be confined to the matters that were raised in the statements that were adduced under 92 ter for the purposes of this part of his testimony, and it may be that issues will arise subsequently in the course of the evidence which might require his return for cross-examination on other matters. So I thought I ought to place that on the record at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Emmerson, any request in this respect as far as Mr. Kelly required not to speak with anyone about --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Same for you, Mr. Harvey?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Same for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Kelly, I would like to thank you. You are excused, as you may have just heard from Mr. Emmerson. The Defence does not exclude for the possibility that they would like to put further questions to you, but you're not limited, meanwhile, in discussing with others your testimony. At the same time, since this possibility exists, I'd advise you not to do that if there's no good reason to do that. Do you understand the difference between being ordered not to speak with anyone one single word about your testimony and not to engage in any conversations which might bother you at a later stage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then you are excused. Madam Usher, would you please escort Mr. Kelly out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. -- MR. DI FAZIO: Just a couple of matters that don't require the presence of Mr. Kelly, but firstly I understand from our case manager that his unredacted 92 ter statement is now available electronically, and I would like to tender that, if I may, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: And I understand that that is 65 ter 1485.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the unredacted statement would then be ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P370, under seal, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. I may take it that where there are no objections against 368, there are no objections against 370 either. Looking at the body language of Defence counsel, this is confirmed; therefore, 370 is admitted into evidence. MR. DI FAZIO: And I also have the two summaries. Do -- should I read them into the transcript now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well -- MR. DI FAZIO: I'm in Your Honours' --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Mr. Di Fazio, I'd like to leave that ...
